title: TUM Blockchain & AI Hackathon
description: AI agents are starting to act on their own: booking, negotiating, paying. The payment rails for that don't fully exist yet. This hackathon is about building the infrastructure and applications that let autonomous agents transact safely and instantly on-chain. Pick a track, build against the partner's challenge, and compete for its prize pool. TUM Blockchain Club has brought together 3,000+ builders, researchers and founders over the last four years, running Europe's largest student-led Web3 event. This year the hackathon sits inside TBC26: three days, two venues, one community, with the main conference and Bundesblock's Digital Assets Day running alongside. title: CODERAVE 2.0
description:
CODE • COLLABORATE • INNOVATE - The SLIET Annual  Hackathon. Organized by Internwell SLIET Club

Venue:
 Sant Longowal Institute of Engineering and Technology (SLIET), Longowal, Punjab

Mode:
 Hybrid — Online (All India) + Offline (SLIET Campus) Coderave 2.0 is a national-level hybrid hackathon designed to bring together innovative minds, passionate developers, designers, and problem-solvers to transform ideas into impactful technology solutions. Organized by Internwell SLIET Club, this edition offers students an opportunity to demonstrate their creativity, technical expertise, teamwork, and problem-solving abilities through a competitive, time-bound development experience. The hackathon welcomes teams from colleges and universities across India through its online participation track, while SLIET students can participate in the offline campus track. Shortlisted teams will present their ideas through PPT pitches, followed by an intensive 24-hour open-source development challenge in which participants will build, test, and demonstrate their solutions. Whether you are interested in web development, app development, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, data science, or other emerging technologies, Coderave 2.0 is your platform to innovate, collaborate, and compete. Round 1 — Registration and PPT Submission:
 The Team Leader registers the complete team and submits the project proposal PPT. Round 2 — PPT Evaluation and Shortlisting:
 Judges evaluate submissions based on innovation, problem relevance, feasibility, technical approach, potential impact, and presentation quality. Round 3 — PPT Pitch:
 Shortlisted online teams(Max 20 team) pitch through an online meeting. Shortlisted SLIET teams pitch offline on campus on 13 February. Round 4 — 24-Hour Open-Source Hackathon:
 Selected teams(Both online and offline track) build their solutions within the official development window. Round 5 — Final Submission and Evaluation:
 Teams submit their working solution, source code repository, demo video, and other required deliverables. Judges evaluate the final projects and announce the winners. The hackathon is an opportunity to turn ideas into functional prototypes within 24 hours. Teams are expected to develop their solutions during the official event window and use open-source tools, libraries, and technologies wherever possible. Participants must maintain a project repository, provide clear documentation, and ensure that their work is demonstrable. Teams must disclose third-party components and follow applicable open-source licences. Previously developed work must be declared, and the core solution must comply with the organizers' originality requirements. Exciting prizes, goodies, certificates, and recognition await outstanding teams. Final awards, prize amounts, sponsor benefits, and certificate eligibility will be announced through the official event communication. Note:
 The dates above are provisional until officially confirmed. The year, registration deadline, online pitch schedule, and final evaluation schedule will be published by the organizers. Bring your idea, build your team, and turn innovation into impact. Register for Coderave 2.0 and take your first step toward creating something extraordinary. Organized by Internwell SLIET Club

Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur, Kerala Prizes:
 Exciting prizes; details to be announced

Team size:
 2–4 participants

Participation:
 Free, including the listed meals Build real solutions. Solve meaningful problems. Create something that works. HAXFINITY is the 24-hour hackathon conducted as part of XTHRON ’26, the annual IT fest of the Department of Computer Science, Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur. Across the event, students from different colleges and backgrounds will come together to identify problems, develop software solutions, build prototypes, and demonstrate their work to a panel of judges. The 24-hour event includes the opening ceremony, a 21-hour building window, project demonstrations, judging, and closing. There is no compulsory theme. Participants are free to choose a problem and develop a software solution using any suitable technology. Whether you are an experienced developer or participating in your first hackathon, HAXFINITY is a space to learn, collaborate, experiment, and build. Prize details and award categories will be announced once confirmed. Build something that solves a problem—or explore an idea you want to bring to life. You may work in education, healthcare, finance, agriculture, entertainment, productivity, cybersecurity, accessibility, sustainability, or any other domain. There is no fixed problem statement or prescribed technology. Choose a problem or idea, design your approach, and build a prototype. Explore intelligent systems and AI-powered applications. Use machine learning, generative AI, natural language processing, computer vision, recommendation systems, data analysis, or other AI-related technologies. Demonstrate how the technology works, explain your implementation, and show what your team built during the event. Possible areas include rural development, accessibility, mental health, financial inclusion, education, healthcare, environmental protection, and community welfare. Focus on understanding the intended users and demonstrating how your prototype could address their needs. Detailed judging criteria and any track-specific award requirements will be published before the event.
* Building window: 21 hours, from 11:00 AM on 12 December to 8:00 AM on 13 December. Meals, rest breaks, mentoring, and activities take place during the building window; they do not pause or extend the submission deadline. Check-in instructions and any final schedule updates will be shared with registered participants. Every competing team will receive the same official building window. HAXFINITY welcomes students from all academic streams and colleges. Students from computer science, information technology, engineering, science, commerce, management, design, and other disciplines are encouraged to participate. Come prepared to learn, collaborate, experiment, and contribute to your team. Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous)

Nilambur, Malappuram, Kerala — 679329 Directions, check-in instructions, and information about travel and overnight arrangements will be shared with registered participants.
